title: Module 6 assessment
subtitle: Data Management & Presentation
description: Fifteen questions across the whole of Module 6. Every question explains its answer, right or wrong.

questions.question: A Table's Total Row uses SUM, so it keeps showing the whole dataset even when the Table is filtered.
questions.explanation: It uses SUBTOTAL, which is why the total respects filters - filter to one region and the total follows. A plain SUM underneath would keep showing the whole-dataset figure while the visible rows say otherwise.

questions.question: What does `Sales[Revenue]` refer to?
options: The Revenue column of the Table named Sales
questions.explanation: Structured references name the Table and the column, and they grow as rows are added. They also read like English, so a formula can be checked by someone who did not write it.

questions.question: Inside a Table, write the calculated-column formula for a row's revenue from its Units and UnitPrice columns.
questions.explanation: The @ means 'this row'. Type it once and Excel fills the whole column and keeps filling it as rows are added - no dragging, and no range to re-point next month.

questions.question: You need to sort departments as Sales, Operations, Finance, HR - not alphabetically. What do you use?
options: A Custom List, then sort by it
questions.explanation: Define the order once under File > Options > Advanced > Edit Custom Lists and it is available to every sort and to AutoFill. The helper-column trick works but has to be rebuilt each time.

questions.question: A slicer can drive several pivot tables at once.
questions.explanation: Through Report Connections, which is where dashboards usually go wrong - a slicer attaches only to the pivots you tick, and an unticked one keeps showing unfiltered figures beside the filtered ones.

questions.question: You set Data Validation to a five-item list, and a week later invalid values appear in the column. How?
options: Someone pasted values in - paste bypasses validation entirely
Validation only checks the first row
questions.explanation: Validation checks typing, not pasting, and it does not re-check existing values. Circle Invalid Data on the Data Validation menu finds what got through.

questions.question: In formula-based conditional formatting over A2:G50, which reference style highlights the whole row based on column E?
questions.explanation: Lock the column and leave the row free, so every cell in the row tests the same column E while the rule moves down. $E$2 tests one cell for all 350 cells; E2 drifts sideways as well as down.

questions.question: Why set a data bar's minimum to Number 0 rather than Automatic?
options: On Automatic the shortest bar is drawn at the lowest value in the range, so the worst item can appear half full
It is required for negative numbers
questions.explanation: Automatic scales between the smallest and largest present, which exaggerates small differences and understates how close to zero the worst case is. Anchoring at 0 makes the bars mean what they look like.

questions.question: Stop If True halts every lower-priority rule on that cell, including data bars.
questions.explanation: Which is why a row-colour rule with Stop If True can make your data bars vanish. If you want both, the data bar must sit above those rules in the list.

questions.question: You need to extract records matching a complex set of conditions to another sheet, repeatedly, each month. Advanced Filter or AutoFilter and copy?
options: Advanced Filter - it writes the matching records out and takes a criteria range you can edit
questions.explanation: Advanced Filter's criteria live in cells, so next month's change is an edit rather than a re-click. In the criteria range, conditions on the same row mean AND and conditions on different rows mean OR.

questions.question: What makes a drop-down list dependent on another cell's choice?
options: A list source using INDIRECT on the first cell's value, with named ranges per category
Two validations on the same cell
questions.explanation: Name a range for each category to match the parent's values, then set the child's source to =INDIRECT(parent cell). Pick Sales and the second list shows only Sales roles.

questions.question: Someone's SUM range has to be re-pointed every month when rows are added. What should they have done?
options: Convert the data to a Table and reference the column
Add blank rows at the bottom in advance
questions.explanation: A Table absorbs new rows and everything pointing at it follows - formulas, pivots, charts. It removes a whole class of monthly maintenance, which is the real reason to use Tables rather than the banding.

questions.question: Sorting one column on its own can scramble a dataset.
questions.explanation: If Excel does not detect the surrounding data, or you expand to the wrong range, names stay put while salaries move - and the sheet still looks perfectly tidy. Sorting inside a Table makes this impossible.

questions.question: A date filter offers 'This Month' and 'Last Month' options. What must be true of the column?
options: It must be in a Table
Excel must hold the values as real dates, not text
questions.explanation: Text that looks like a date gets text filters only. The date filters appearing is itself a quick confirmation that the column is genuinely numeric.

questions.question: Rule order matters when two conditional formats could apply to the same cell. Which wins?
options: The one higher in the Manage Rules list
questions.explanation: Priority runs top-down in Manage Rules, and you reorder with the arrows. Put the most serious condition first - Critical should outrank Low, or a critical row quietly shows as merely low.
